ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function \(y = x + b\) intersects the x-axis and the y-axis at points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively, and intersects the graph of the direct proportionality function \(y = -2x\) at point \(C\), where the y-coordinate of point \(C\) is \(4\). If a moving point \(P\) is on the ray \(CA\), and the area of triangle \(OAP\) is \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the area of triangle \(OBC\), what are the coordinates of point \(P\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $P\left(x, x+6\right)$,\\
when $S_{\triangle OAP}=\frac{1}{8}S_{\triangle OBC}$, then $\frac{1}{2}AO\cdot |x|=\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{2}\times BO\cdot |y_c|$,\\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}\times 6|x|=\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 4$, hence $x=\pm \frac{1}{2}$,\\
Moreover, since the moving point P is on the ray $CA$,\\
$\therefore x\ge -2$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point P are $\boxed{P_{1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{11}{2}\right)}$, $\boxed{P_{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{13}{2}\right)}$.

raw_record.original_question: In the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function \(y = x + b\) intersects the x-axis and the y-axis at points \(A\) and \(B\) respectively, and intersects the graph of the direct proportionality function \(y = -2x\) at point \(C\), where the y-coordinate of point \(C\) is \(4\). If a moving point \(P\) is on the ray \(CA\), and the area of triangle \(OAP\) is \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the area of triangle \(OBC\), what are the coordinates of point \(P\)?
raw_record.answer: Let \(P\left(x, x+6\right)\). When \(S_{\triangle OAP}=\frac{1}{8}S_{\triangle OBC}\), then \(\frac{1}{2}AO\cdot |x|=\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{2}\times BO\cdot |y_c|\). Therefore, \(\frac{1}{2}\times 6|x|=\frac{1}{8}\times \frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 4\), hence \(x=\pm \frac{1}{2}\). Moreover, since the moving point \(P\) is on the ray \(CA\), \(x\ge -2\). Therefore the coordinates of point \(P\) are \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{11}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{13}{2}\right)\).

In the figure, the line y=x+b is a line slanting upward to the right; its intersection point with the y-axis is labeled A, and its intersection point with the left side of the x-axis is labeled B; another line y=-2x passes through the origin O and intersects y=x+b at C. According to the figure labels and the specified method, A is the y-axis intercept point, and B is the x-axis intercept point.

Because C is on y=-2x, and the y-coordinate of C is 4, 4=-2x, giving x=-2, so C=(-2,4). Also C is on y=x+b, so 4=-2+b, giving b=6, and the line is y=x+6.

From the figure label, A is the y-axis intercept point, so A=(0,6); B is the x-axis intercept point, so let y=0, giving x=-6, namely B=(-6,0). Let P be on the line y=x+6, then P=(x,x+6). Since P is on ray CA, the ray extends upward to the right from C(-2,4) through A(0,6), so x>=-2 is required.

In triangle OAP, OA is on the y-axis, length OA=6, and the horizontal distance from point P to the y-axis is |x|, so S_{triangle OAP}=1/2*6*|x|=3|x|. In triangle OBC, OB is on the x-axis, length OB=6, and the y-coordinate of point C is 4, so the height is 4, S_{triangle OBC}=1/2*6*4=12.

From the problem statement S_{triangle OAP}=1/8 S_{triangle OBC}, so 3|x|=12/8=3/2, giving |x|=1/2, therefore x=±1/2. Both values satisfy x>=-2. Substituting into y=x+6, get that when x=-1/2, y=11/2; when x=1/2, y=13/2.
